sections.h2: Where to take a deed in Van Buren County
sections.html:
Paperwork for Van Buren County land goes to the Register of Deeds in Suite 102 at 219 E. Paw Paw Street, Paw Paw. The counter is open weekdays from 8:30 in the morning to 5:00 in the afternoon and closed on holidays. Call (269) 657-8242 with questions.

The office accepts originals bearing real signatures and court papers that carry a certification. Photocopies and faxes are refused.

Clerks read each paper against state requirements, scan and index it, then hand the original back to the sender. The county promises a turnaround of one to two days for a compliant paper. When a title company runs your closing, that company gets the original first, so ask them when it will be passed along to you.

A single flat price covers any length of deed or mortgage, and the figures match MCL 600.2567.

Walk-in and mailed recording payments must be cash or a check written to Register of Deeds. A card is accepted only for copies bought online. Mail a stamped return envelope with your package so the original finds its way back.

sections.h2: When a deed needs the treasurer's stamp first
sections.html:
Warranty deeds, land contracts and assignments that carry a warranty promise must arrive with a county treasurer's tax certificate. The rule traces to MCL 211.135, which wants proof that five years of taxes before the instrument date are paid and a statement on tax liens or tax titles. Quitclaim deeds without warranty covenants escape it.

  • Get the certificate before you head to Paw Paw, because the recording desk will refuse a warranty deed without it.
  • Budget $5.00 for it in addition to the $30.00 recording price.
  • Any unpaid tax usually comes out of your proceeds, so ask the county treasurer for the figure early enough to plan the closing date.

sections.h2: How does transfer tax work on a house sale?
sections.html:
The seller pays when value reaches $100.00. The county rate is $0.55 and the state rate is $3.75, each applied to every $500 or fraction of $500, under MCL 207.504 and MCL 207.525.

Show the full price on the deed or file a Real Estate Transfer Valuation Affidavit, which is free. For swaps, each deed is taxed on its own property's real value. A parcel that straddles county lines needs a price per parcel and a payment to each county.

Delivery of the deed starts a 15-day clock for paying the county treasurer under MCL 207.523. A sale later found exempt can be refunded through the state Treasury, provided the form goes in within four years of payment.

Some transfers are exempt under MCL 207.526, such as these:

  • Gifts from a parent to a child, stepchild or adopted child.
  • Gifts from a grandparent to a grandchild.
  • Corrective deeds that confirm title the buyer already has.
  • Court orders that move property with no stated price.

sections.h2: What the office asks for by document type
sections.html:
Every paper needs a date and a legal description. Beyond that, the requirements differ by document type, and two stand out for sellers dealing with a distressed property.

  • A sheriff's sale or foreclosure by advertisement comes with the auction sale amount, a signed and notarized auctioneer statement, a Soldiers and Sailors affidavit if it applies, the newspaper publication notice, an affidavit of posting, a redemption period statement and an affidavit of redemption.
  • A tax deed or similar paper carries the $5.00 treasurer certificate.
  • Releases and assignments cross-reference the original by liber and page.
  • A land patent must be an original or certified copy.

General rules track MCL 565.201. Names are typed under signatures and match the notary block, every party's address appears, the drafter is identified and the notary acknowledgment is complete. Leave 2 1/2 inches clear at the top of page one, use 10-point type or bigger and keep sheets to 8.5 by 14 inches at most. Wrong fees, missing drafter names, handwritten names and partial notary certificates are the usual causes of rejection.

A certified death certificate must back any deed that names a survivor. The office cannot draft documents or give legal advice, so see a lawyer or title agent for wording.

The Register of Deeds portal at deeds.vanburencountymi.gov lets anyone search the index and buy images one document at a time. A BS&A property search from the county site also lists the liber and page in each legal description, and the sale history section can fill in gaps.

Paying for an older record depends on its volume. Liber 924 or lower is paid through the county's GovPayNow link. Liber 925 and higher is bought from the searchable index and downloads right after payment. Online copy orders may take up to two working days, and big orders on the portal may take up to 48 hours. Recorded papers are public, so anyone can request a copy of any deed.

sections.h2: Selling a home in Van Buren County
sections.html:
The county covers 1,090 square miles, 482 of them water, with farmland, small towns and lakeshore making up the rest. Paw Paw is the seat. Bangor, Gobles, Hartford and part of South Haven are cities, while Decatur, Lawton, Mattawan, Lawrence, Bloomingdale and Paw Paw are villages. Antwerp and Almena townships, beside Kalamazoo County, are turning suburban.

Many inland lakes are ringed by year-round homes and cottages, and Lake Michigan beaches, Van Buren State Park and the Kal-Haven Trail draw visitors. Highways include I-94, I-196, US 31 and M-40, and an Amtrak Pere Marquette stop serves the county.

Of 30,622 households, 80.6 percent own. Owner-occupied homes are valued at $206,500 at the median, and gross rent runs $870. Zoning and building permits come from the township or city, so call the local hall about those before you list.

Plan the paperwork backward from closing day: order the treasurer's certificate, confirm the transfer tax with the title agent, and make sure the deed meets the format rules above. A cash buyer closes quickly, but the recording desk works at the same pace either way.

faqs.q: What is the recording price in Van Buren County?
faqs.a: $30.00 per instrument, whatever the page count. Add $3.00 for each further instrument assigned or discharged. Certified copies and treasurer tax certificates cost $5.00, and photocopies cost $1.00 a page.

faqs.q: Does the Van Buren County Register of Deeds take credit cards?
faqs.a: Only for copies ordered online. Anything you file, along with the transfer tax, must be paid in cash or by check made out to Register of Deeds.

faqs.q: Who owes transfer tax on a Van Buren County sale?
faqs.a: The seller, when the property's value is $100.00 or more. County tax is $0.55 and state tax is $3.75 for each $500 or fraction of $500.

faqs.q: How fast does the Van Buren County office record a deed?
faqs.a: Within one to two days of receipt, if the paper meets the requirements. Wrong fees, missing drafter names, handwritten names and incomplete notary certificates get it sent back.

faqs.q: Is a treasurer's certificate needed for a Van Buren County quitclaim deed?
faqs.a: No. Warranty deeds, land contracts and assignments with a warranty covenant need it. A quitclaim deed without warranty covenants is excused under MCL 211.135.
